findings.problem: The two bullets at lines 171–191 do the same nontrivial transfer step as the matching branches in three other proofs. They (1) pick the profile time t from `hprofiles`, (2) normalise `baseEquiv (baseEquiv.symm x)`, (3) instantiate a G-quantified hypothesis (`havoid` or `hcross`) at G = `phaseRealChartMap i e.symm W`, using smoothness from `hW.1` and the closeness bound weakened from δ to η, and (4) use `phaseGauss_isometry` or `phaseMetricRead_isometry_det` to convert the curvature or Gram-determinant side condition from the target-metric chart read to the realised immersion. The `hDH` bullet repeats steps (1), (2) and (4) with the extra `coordinateGauss_eq_curvature_mul` bridge. The curve bullet (lines 171–178) is identical, modulo `min_le_right _ _` versus `hδη`, to IndependentCircularCurves.lean lines 110–117. The whole proof is also a verbatim copy of ExactCircularBoundary.lean lines 147–192 with `data.A` replaced by `A₀`. A fix to the transfer logic, such as the curvature direction or the choice of `t`, must therefore be made in at least four places.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one atlas-level lemma, with no `MetricGoodPhaseData`, in `SmoothingAtlas` (for example in PhaseMetricRead.lean or a new small file). It would state that, for `A`, `i`, `hi : ContDiff ℝ ∞ e.symm`, `hW : IsSmoothIsometricImmersion M h W` and `hactive : A.chartWeight i (e.symm (baseEquiv.symm x)) ≠ 0`, the following holds. Let `Pre G p` be an arbitrary predicate on (G, p) in which `ContDiff ℝ ∞ G` is already a premise, and let `Q` be the conclusion. If `hP : ∀ G, ContDiff ℝ ∞ G → ∀ p, ‖realBoundaryProfile G z p - surfaceCircularProfile (A.phaseRealChartMap i e.symm F) a e₁ e₂ α (x,t)‖ < η → k ≤ coordinateGauss (realMetric G dx dx) (realMetric G dx dy) (realMetric G dy dy) p → Q G p`, together with `herror : ‖realBoundaryProfile (A.phaseRealChartMap i e.symm W) z x - surfaceCircularProfile … (x,t)‖ < δ`, `hδη : δ ≤ η`, and `hk : k ≤ coordinateGauss (fun y => A.phaseMetricRead i e.symm h y 0) (fun y => A.phaseMetricRead i e.symm h y 1) (fun y => A.phaseMetricRead i e.symm h y 2) x`, then `Q (A.phaseRealChartMap i e.symm W) x`. Proof: `exact hP _ (A.phaseRealChartMap_smooth i hi hW.1) x (herror.trans_le hδη) (by rw [A.phaseGauss_isometry i hi hW hactive]; exact hk)`.

Add a second lemma, `phase_gram_det_ne_zero`, for `hdetE`. It would take `hdetE` and `hactiveE` and conclude `gramDet (coordDeriv dx H x) (coordDeriv dy H x) ≠ 0` for `H = phaseRealChartMap i e.symm W`. Its proof is the existing `rw [phaseMetricRead_isometry_det …]; exact hdetE x hx`.

Better, factor the whole post-processing of `hprofiles` into one lemma, `circular_boundary_of_profiles`. It would take the already-obtained `hprofiles`, the hypotheses `havoid`, `hcross`, `hcurv`, `hcurvE`, `hdetE`, `hactive` and `hactiveE`, and the bounds δ ≤ η and z < η, and conclude the curve and ordered-crossing conjuncts. Then lines 171–191 reduce to `exact A₀.circular_boundary_of_profiles … hprofiles …`, and the same lemma closes the corresponding bullets in ExactCircularBoundary.lean (with `data.A`) and, for the curve part, in IndependentCircularCurves.lean and ExactCircularCurves.lean. The independent theorem keeps its `data.independent_exact_circular_primitive_profiles` call, and the exact one keeps `data.exact_circular_primitive_profiles`. The shared lemma needs neither `houter` nor `data`.
findings.benefit: The curvature and Gram-determinant transfer is stated and proved once instead of four times. Each of the two Boundary theorems then reads as: obtain profiles, extract regularity, apply the lemma. A reader can see what is specific to each theorem (which profiles lemma supplies `hprofiles`, and whether `houter` is needed) without comparing 20 near-identical lines across files. Future changes, such as a different δ/η bookkeeping or another side condition on the Gauss curvature, are made once.
